traceability.evidence:
Implementation: - Core rule: src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts - JSDoc explicitly links to story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md with @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION and REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE. - meta: type="problem", docs.description="Require @story and @req annotations on code branches", fixable="code". - messages.missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.", providing clear, parameterized error text. - schema supports a branchTypes array option, enforcing ESLint best-practice schema validation. - create(context): calls validateBranchTypes(context) to either get a list of branch types or a configuration-error listener; registers handlers for each branch type, skipping unlabeled SwitchCase defaults and delegating detection/reporting to reportMissingAnnotations.
- Helpers: src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts - DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES defines significance criteria for branches: IfStatement, SwitchCase, TryStatement, CatchClause, ForStatement, ForOfStatement, ForInStatement, WhileStatement, DoWhileStatement (annotated with @story 004 and REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA). - validateBranchTypes(context) (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE): - If options.branchTypes is omitted: returns DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES. - If options.branchTypes is a subset of DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES: returns that array. - If any invalid type is present: returns a RuleListener with a Program handler that reports, for each invalid type, a message of the form: Value "" should be equal to one of the allowed values: . - gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node) (REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION): - For SwitchCase: scans up to 2 lines above for line/block comments via regex, collecting and joining their text. - For all other branch types: uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) and joins comment.value strings. - getBranchAnnotationInfo(...) (internal, supports REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): - text = gatherBranchCommentText(...); - missingStory = !/@story\b/.test(text); missingReq = !/@req\b/.test(text); - computes indent and insertion position for fixes from sourceCode and node.loc. - reportMissingStory(...) and reportMissingReq(...) (REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): - Emit missingAnnotation errors specifying missing "@story" or "@req". - Provide fixers that insert `// @story .story.md` or `// @req ` above the branch where appropriate, with logic to avoid multiple story autofixes. - reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef): - Uses getBranchAnnotationInfo and then conditionally invokes reportMissingStory/reportMissingReq for each missing annotation, handling multiple missing cases for a single branch.
Tests (all passing in `npm test -- --verbose`): - Rule behavior: tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts - Annotated with @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md. - Uses RuleTester to cover: - Valid cases demonstrating correct detection of annotated branches across all significant branch types: - IfStatement, SwitchCase (including inline and with preceding comments and with a blank line), TryStatement (try/finally and try/catch), CatchClause, ForStatement, ForOfStatement, ForInStatement, WhileStatement, DoWhileStatement. - Default SwitchCase explicitly allowed without annotations (ensuring significance criteria distinction). - Custom branchTypes options showing unlisted branch types are ignored and only configured ones enforced. - Invalid cases ensuring detection and autofix: - Missing annotations on if, for, while, switch-case, do-while, for-of, for-in, and try-catch, with expected output matching inserted `// @story .story.md` and/or `// @req ` as implemented by helpers. - Configuration error case with options: [{ branchTypes: ["UnknownType"] }] expecting an error matching /should be equal to one of the allowed values/, verifying invalid-config handling.
- Helper configuration tests: tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts - Verify validateBranchTypes returns DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES by default, returns provided valid branchTypes array unchanged, and returns a listener that calls context.report once per invalid type with messages including `Value "" should be equal to one of the allowed values:`.
Integration into plugin and presets (ensures rule is available and used as intended): - src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes "require-branch-annotation" so rule is dynamically loaded. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps "traceability/require-branch-annotation" to "error". - Flat configs (recommended and strict) created via createTraceabilityFlatConfig() include this rule with severity "error". - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts - Asserts rules object contains "require-branch-annotation" in the expected key list. - Verifies configs.recommended[0].rules has "traceability/require-branch-annotation": "error" and that strict has the same mapping.
Documentation: - docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md - Explicitly references @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE. - Describes behavior: checks JSDoc or inline comments immediately preceding significant branches and requires both @story and @req. - Documents branchTypes option, its default/allowed values aligned with DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES, and describes invalid configuration behavior with example error message. - Provides correct and incorrect code examples plus an invalid-configuration example.
Global tests: - Full Jest run (`npm test -- --verbose`) reports: - PASS tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts - PASS tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts - PASS tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts - Overall: 35 test suites, 266 tests passed, 0 failed.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are satisfied: - Core Functionality: The require-branch-annotation rule, together with branch-annotation-helpers, detects missing @story/@req annotations on significant branch types (if/else, try/catch, switch cases, and loops) and can autofix by inserting placeholder annotations where appropriate. Tests cover each branch type with both valid and invalid scenarios. - Quality Standards: The rule follows ESLint best practices (meta schema, message IDs, clear separation of configuration validation, and helper utilities) and is implemented in a performance-conscious way (limited SwitchCase scanning and only registering handlers for configured node types). - Integration: The rule is exported via the plugin’s dynamic rule loading, and is included in both recommended and strict flat-config presets with severity 'error'. Integration tests confirm the rule name and configuration appear in plugin exports and presets. - User Experience: Error messages clearly indicate which annotation is missing ("@story" or "@req") and are tied to the specific branch node, satisfying the need for clear feedback about which branch requires annotation and why. - Error Handling: Invalid branchTypes configuration is handled gracefully by returning a Program listener that reports descriptive errors for each invalid value. Edge cases such as default switch cases and switch cases with blank lines before comments are covered by targeted logic and tests, and try/catch ensures both branches are checked. - Documentation: A dedicated rule doc (docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md) exists, linked to this story, with explanation, configuration details, and examples of correct, incorrect, and invalid-configuration usage. The rule is also mentioned in README as part of available rules. Given the implemented code, comprehensive targeted tests, integration tests, and documentation all aligned with docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md, this story is fully implemented and validated.
